Meeting header: 2027-01-05 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Carmen Lopez (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Rowan Ellis (Redwood CSM), Jordan Meyers (Brighton VP Platform), Priya Anand (Brighton Head of Security), Ethan Cole (Brighton SRE), Lina Park (Brighton Procurement)

Summary:
- Brighton is evaluating a renewal with a short bridge term tied to an on-prem pilot and an EU region burst capability. They want clearer pricing on burst vs reserved, and assurance on KMS/HSM integration and SOC 2 artifacts. Redwood to run benchmarks and provide amended contract language.

Topics: contract amendment, on-prem pilot scope, EU regional capacity, KMS/HSM and data residency, performance benchmarks, pricing tiers and discounts, timeline for sign-off.

Action items (high level above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Carmen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off — Rowan, Maya, you good?
[00:05] Rowan: Yep all set. Hi Brighton team, good to see you.
[00:10] Jordan: Hi, thanks for doing this. We're roughly 45 minutes if that's ok, we have a few folks who need to hop after.
[00:15] Carmen: Perfect. Today we want to align on the renewal ask you sent last week: a short extension, a pilot for on-prem, and EU burst capacity for peak inference. We'll cover tech, security, and pricing. Maya will cover the bench and pilot requirements.
[00:27] Maya: Great, I'll share my screen in a sec. (screen noise) Okay, so quick recap of what we heard: Brighton wants a six month bridge renewal to avoid churn, start an on-prem pilot for regulated workloads, and provision additional capacity in eu-west for peak hours with burst buckets — correct me if I'm off.
[00:42] Jordan: That's right. The six months keeps ops stable while our legal finalizes the procurement. The EU bursts are critical for the new product launch in March.
[00:50] Priya: One more thing on EU: data must remain in-region, encryption keys — we have an HSM requirement, ideally FIPS 140-2/3 compatible.
[00:58] Maya: Got it, HSM and key control. We support customer-managed KMS in our private deployment and can integrate with an HSM chain — I'll outline options.
[01:05] Ethan: For performance we care about P95 latency under 120ms for our inference path; cost sensitivity at token-level is high, so we need cost per token estimates for both hosted bursts and on-prem.
[01:18] Carmen: Understood. I'll run pricing scenarios after Maya provides throughput numbers.
[01:22] Lina: From procurement: the amendment needs simple billing changes and a clause for the pilot that doesn't change the long-term commitment unless we move to production.
[01:30] Carmen: We can do a pilot clause. We'll propose a bridge with option to convert committed capacity within the six months at a pre-agreed uplift.
[01:36] Maya: Quick note on kernels and quantization: for Llama2-style weights we recommend the 8-bit quantized variant for cost during the pilot; we'll provide a tested config that still meets quality SLOs.
[01:46] Jordan: Any quality tradeoffs with 8-bit? We've got sensitive classification pipelines.
[01:51] Maya: Minor diffs on some edge cases; our evals show <2% regressed answers on our validation set for general completion. For classification we can run the benchmark on your prompt set — that's one of the next steps.
[02:03] Priya: And what about logging? We need audit logs, IAM, RBAC and an immutable audit trail for model access.
[02:10] Rowan: Our private deployment includes audit logs and configurable retention. We can expose token-level tracing to your SIEM and tie into SSO.
[02:15] Jordan: Good. Can you summarize the two deployment options we discussed and the fallback?
[02:20] Maya: Sure — hosted (Redwood API) with EU-region burst buckets: fastest to start, pay-as-you-go, but we control the keys. Dedicated reserved pools: isolated capacity on Redwood-managed infra with higher SLA. Private on-prem: you run the control plane or we can provide an appliance — full key control, HSM integration. Fallbacks: policy-based routing to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
[02:39] Ethan: How does KV cache behave across on-prem and hosted? We have long conversation histories.
[02:45] Maya: KV is local to the runtime; for hybrid deployments we can deploy a shared cache in the regional VPC or enable prefix caching at the application layer. We'll outline latency tradeoffs.
[02:59] Speaker 3: (inaudible) sorry — did you say shared cache would add network hops?
[03:03] Maya: Yes, slight increase but still within acceptable tail latencies if deployed in the same AZ.
[03:10] Jordan: Okay, pricing — we need a sample of three scenarios: 1) six-month bridge with reserved small pool + EU burst, 2) immediate on-prem pilot + hosted fallback, 3) convert to annual committed at end of pilot.
[03:23] Carmen: We'll put those in a pricing table. Lina, anything else from procurement on contract language?
[03:28] Lina: Just assert clarity on SLAs and termination rights for the pilot. Also we need a data processing addendum.
[03:36] Carmen: We have a standard DPA and can make the pilot termination point non-penalizing.
[03:40] Priya: For security review, I will need SOC 2 Type II report and an architecture diagram showing where keys are stored in each deployment mode.
[03:48] Rowan: We'll share the SOC 2 artifact package and a redacted arch diagram. Also we'll include details for HSM options (Cloud HSM, Thales via our connectors, or customer HSM).
[03:59] Ethan: On the benchmark you mentioned, what load shape will you run? Peak spikiness matters.
[04:05] Maya: We'll mirror your p95/p99 mix, but propose a two-stage: synthetic ramp tests (48 hours) and a short real traffic replay if you can provide anonymized traces.
[04:15] Jordan: We can do anonymized replay — developers can extract a 48hr sample.
[04:20] Maya: Great. We'll need one contact for SRE to coordinate.
[04:24] Ethan: That's me.
[04:26] Carmen: Ok timeline check — Carmen: We'll send pricing and the amendment by Monday (2027-01-10). Maya: benchmark plan by 2027-01-12. Rowan: on-prem checklist by 2027-01-14. Jordan: internal sign-off target 2027-01-20. Does that work?
[04:41] Jordan: Yes.
[04:43] Priya: Quick question on encryption in transit — do you support TLS mutual auth for control plane?
[04:48] Maya: Yes, mutual TLS for control plane is supported in Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer TLS with customer cert pinning for VPC peering.
[04:57] Jordan: How much runway do we have if production gets busy in March? Suppose traffic doubles.
[05:03] Carmen: Reserved pools can be bumped with short-notice burst credits; we can provision scheduled capacity in EU assuming we agree on a lead time — normally 2–3 weeks for larger GPUs. We'll propose a burst bucket to absorb spikes for up to 48 hours while provisioning scales.
[05:16] Lina: Pricing on burst buckets — is that a premium?
[05:19] Carmen: Yes, bursts have a higher per-token rate. But we can tier it: small burst at moderate premium, larger emergency burst at higher premium. We'll model three tiers in the pricing sheet.
[05:30] Jordan: Any risk around model parity across hosted and on-prem? We don't want different outputs in prod vs pilot.
[05:36] Maya: We support pinned model versions and identical quantization kernels. However, tiny differences in GPU kernels and tensor cores can change floating point — we'll aim to match via the same runtime and provide a regression harness to validate parity on your prompt set.
[05:50] Priya: Does Redwood capture model provenance for audit? We need a record of model version, weights hash, and rollout history.
[05:56] Rowan: Yes, model provenance and rollout audit are standard in our console and included for Private deployments. We'll export artifacts for compliance.
[06:04] Jordan: Sounds good. On the contract conversion: if we convert to an annual commitment post-pilot, can we lock pricing for 12 months?
[06:11] Carmen: Yes, conversion price lock is standard. We'll set conversion terms in the amendment.
[06:16] Ethan: One last technical: can we test quantized vs fp16 on identical prompts? We want to measure latency/cost and quality tradeoffs.
[06:23] Maya: Absolutely — we'll include fp16 and 8-bit runs in the bench. We'll provide latency percentiles and quality diffs on your classification set.
[06:31] Speaker 2: (background) 
[06:34] Carmen: Ok we're approaching time, I'll summarize. Next steps: Redwood to send pricing table + amendment (Carmen), Maya to send benchmark plan and run scripts (Maya), Rowan to deliver on-prem checklist and SOC 2 artifacts (Rowan), Brighton to confirm pilot stakeholders and provide anonymized trace (Jordan/Ethan).
[06:52] Jordan: Thanks, this is helpful. We want to avoid surprises on cost — so please be explicit on burst rates.
[06:58] Lina: And include termination language for the pilot and DPA.
[07:02] Carmen: Will do. Anything else?
[07:05] Priya: I'll review the KMS options and send the HSM requirements doc.
[07:09] Carmen: Great. We'll reconvene after the pricing doc — propose Jan 13 for a quick follow-up.
[07:15] Jordan: Jan 13 works. Thanks everyone.
[07:18] Carmen: Thanks — meeting adjourned.
